arxiv-2211-04376.title: Lasing modes in ZnO nanowires coupled to planar metals
arxiv-2211-04376.creator: Daniel Repp, Angela Barreda, Francesco Vitale, Isabelle Staude, Ulf Peschel, Carsten Ronning, Thomas Pertsch
arxiv-2211-04376.description: Abstract Semiconductor nanowire lasers can be subject to modifications of their lasing threshold resulting from a variation of their environment. A promising choice is to use metallic substrates to gain access to low-volume Surface-Plasmon-Polariton (SPP) modes. We introduce a simple, yet quantitatively precise model that can serve to describe mode competition in nanowire lasers on metallic substrates.

arxiv-2306-13030.title: Online Self-Supervised Deep Learning for Intrusion Detection Systems Thanks: This research has been supported in part by the European Commission H2020 Program through the IoTAC Research and Innovation Action under Grant Agreement No. 952684 and by the European Commission Horizon Europe – the Framewo
arxiv-2306-13030.creator: Mert Nakıp, Erol Gelenbe
arxiv-2306-13030.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mert Nakıp, Erol Gelenbe. This paper proposes a novel Self-Supervised Intrusion Detection (SSID) framework, which enables a fully online Deep Learning (DL) based Intrusion Detection System (IDS) that requires no human intervention or prior off-line learning. The proposed framework analyzes and labels incoming traffic packets based only on the decisions of the IDS itself using an Auto-Associative Deep Random Neural Network, and on an online estimate of its statistically measured trustworthiness.

arxiv-2309-07951.title: Non-standard axion electrodynamics and the dual Witten effect
arxiv-2309-07951.creator: Ben Heidenreich, Jacob McNamara, Matthew Reece, [10pt] Department of Physics, University of Massachusetts, Amherst, MA 01003 USA
arxiv-2309-07951.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ben Heidenreich, Jacob McNamara, Matthew Reece, [10pt] Department of Physics, University of Massachusetts, Amherst, MA 01003 USA. Standard axion electrodynamics has two closely related features. First, the coupling of a massless axion field to photons is quantized, in units proportional to the electric gauge coupling squared. Second, the equations of motion tell us that a time-dependent axion field in a background magnetic field sources an effective electric current, but a time-dependent axion field in a background electric field has no effect.

arxiv-2311-07035.title: contHutch++: Stochastic trace estimation for implicit integral operators Thanks: Funding: This work is supported by National Science Foundation grant No. DMS-2045646. The work was also supported by the SciAI Center, and funded by the Office of Naval Research (ONR), under Grant Number N00014-23-1-272
arxiv-2311-07035.creator: Jennifer Zvonek, Andrew Horning, Alex Townsend
arxiv-2311-07035.description: Abstract Hutchinson’s estimator is a randomized algorithm that computes an ϵ \epsilon -approximation to the trace of any positive semidefinite matrix using 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 / ϵ 2 ) \mathcal{O}(1/\epsilon^{2}) matrix-vector products. An improvement of Hutchinson’s estimator, known as Hutch + + + + \Hutch++ , only requires 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 / ϵ ) \mathcal{O}(1/\epsilon) matrix-vector products.

arxiv-2404-06293.creator: Simon Mauras, Divyarthi Mohan, Rebecca Reiffenhäuser
arxiv-2404-06293.description: Abstract We study online selection problems in both the prophet and secretary settings, when arriving agents have interdependent values. In the interdependent values model, introduced in the seminal work of Milgrom and Weber [1982], each agent has a private signal and the value of an agent is a function of the signals held by all agents.

arxiv-2504-07552.title: Uniqueness of supercritical Gaussian multiplicative chaos
arxiv-2504-07552.creator: Federico Bertacco 1, Martin Hairer 2
arxiv-2504-07552.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Federico Bertacco 1, Martin Hairer 2. We show that, for general convolution approximations to a large class of log-correlated Gaussian fields, the properly normalised supercritical Gaussian multiplicative chaos measures converge stably to a nontrivial limit. This limit depends on the choice of regularisation only through a multiplicative constant and can be characterised as an integrated atomic measure with a random intensity expressed in terms of the critical Gaussian multiplicative chaos.

arxiv-2509-08538.title: MESH - Understanding Videos Like Human: Measuring Hallucinations in Large Video Models Conference: ; 2025; MESH CCS: Computing methodologies Video summarization CCS: Computing methodologies Activity recognition and understanding CCS: Computing methodologies Scene understanding
arxiv-2509-08538.creator: Garry Yang, Zizhe Chen, Man Hon Wong, Haoyu Lei, Yongqiang Chen, Zhenguo Li, Kaiwen Zhou, James Cheng
arxiv-2509-08538.description: Abstract . Large Video Models (LVMs) build on the semantic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and vision modules by integrating temporal information to better understand dynamic video content. Despite their progress, LVMs are prone to hallucinations—producing inaccurate or irrelevant descriptions.

arxiv-2510-12683.title: Supercontinuum Generation in 1-decanol
arxiv-2510-12683.creator: Nathan G. Drouillard, 1,* Jacob A. Stephen, 1, Chathurangani Jayalath Arachchige, 1, Jeet Shannigrahi, 2, and TJ Hammond 1
arxiv-2510-12683.description: Abstract Although solids have been recently used in ultrafast experiments for spectral broadening due to their relatively high nonlinearity, their sensitivity to damage limits their long-term stability. Liquids are a possible alternative to solids as a nonlinear medium because of their comparable nonlinearity and resistance to permanent damage.

arxiv-2510-22590.title: ATOM: AdapTive and OptiMized dynamic temporal knowledge graph construction using LLMs
arxiv-2510-22590.creator: Yassir LAIRGI, Ludovic MONCLA, Khalid BENABDESLEM, Rémy CAZABET, Pierre CLÉAU
arxiv-2510-22590.description: Abstract In today’s rapidly expanding data landscape, knowledge extraction from unstructured text is vital for real-time analytics, temporal inference, and dynamic memory frameworks. However, traditional static knowledge graph (KG) construction often overlooks the dynamic and time-sensitive nature of real-world data, limiting adaptability to continuous changes.

pmc-11518199.title: Vaccine literacy and cultural competence training of Professional FOR health to improve the vaccination offer
pmc-11518199.creator: M Russo, G Marchetti, A Gatta, C Bartolucci, I Aloise, N Papaevgeniou, S Declich, M Marceca
pmc-11518199.description: BackgroundIt is essential that healthcare institutions have a high level of organizational vaccine literacy so that they can support Newly Arrived Migrants (NAM) to navigate, understand and make informed decisions on vaccinations in an effort to make uptake equitable. Developing training material for Professional-FOR-health (PfH) working with NAM, i.e. health and non-health workers, can improve the vaccination offer for NAM.

pmc-12467258.title: A Comparative Study on COVID-19 Dynamics: Mathematical Modeling, Predictions, and Resource Allocation Strategies in Romania, Italy, and Switzerland
pmc-12467258.creator: Cristina-Maria Stăncioi, Iulia Adina Ștefan, Violeta Briciu, Vlad Mureșan, Iulia Clitan, Mihail Abrudean, Mihaela-Ligia Ungureșan, Radu Miron, Ecaterina Stativă, Roxana Carmen Cordoș, Adriana Topan, Ioana Nanu, Ivan Ganchev Ivanov
pmc-12467258.description: This research provides valuable insights into the application of mathematical modeling to real-world scenarios, as exemplified by the COVID-19 pandemic. After data collection, the preparation stage included exploratory analysis, standardization and normalization, computation, and validation. A mathematical model initially developed for COVID-19 dynamics in Romania was subsequently applied to data from Italy and Switzerland during the same time interval.

pmc-12529026.title: 24 million years of pollination interaction between European linden flowers and bumble bees
pmc-12529026.creator: Christian Geier, Michael S. Engel, Johannes M. Bouchal, Silvia Ulrich, Jürg Schönenberger, Dieter Uhl, Torsten Wappler, Sonja Wedmann, Loup Boudet, Friðgeir Grímsson
pmc-12529026.description: Summary Pollination is the most common insect–plant mutualism, binding them in a co‐evolutionary framework. Historic evidence of this interaction can be partly inferred from time‐calibrated molecular phylogenies of plant and insect lineages or directly from fossils. Fossils providing such evidence are sparse and only a few fossiliferous localities offer adequate preservation of both flowers and insects.

uslaw-usc-t31-s5134.title: 31 U.S.C. § 5134 — Numismatic Public Enterprise Fund
uslaw-usc-t31-s5134.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t31-s5134.description: United States Code, Title 31 (Money And Finance); Chapter 51 (Coins And Currency); Subchapter III (United States Mint). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Definitions.— For purposes of this section— (1) Fund.— The term “Fund” means the Numismatic Public Enterprise Fund. (2) Mint.— The term “Mint” means the United States Mint. (3) Numismatic item.— The term “numismatic item” means any medal, proof.
